text:
Eric Robinson had the kind of afternoon at Madison Square Garden that fourth-liners remember: a shorthanded goal at 13:00 of the first and an assist on Alexander Nikishin's goal in the second, first star in a 5-2 Carolina win. He played 12:36.

He's an undrafted Princeton grad, now a Stanley Cup winner with Carolina, and his season has been quietly productive: 11 points in 23 games, already well past half of last season's 18 points. Some of that is the company. Carolina has scored 9.4 more goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey notes he plays with strong teammates, which flatters raw numbers.

The five-on-five picture is mixed: the Hurricanes take 57% of the shot attempts with him on but only 49% of the expected goals, and they're much better without him in chance quality.

He's fast: NHL Edge puts his top speed at the 94th percentile among forwards, and 55% of his shots came off the rush last season by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. What to watch: penalty-kill work, where a goal like Sunday's is the bonus.
